chunks: And from him, from Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sadaqah, from Malik ibn 'Atiyyah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever visits al-Husayn (peace be upon him), Allah will register for him eighty purified Hajj.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting Imam Husayn according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) to emphasize the unique status of Karbala as a spiritual axis, equating the visitation of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) with eighty accepted Hajj pilgrimages. This immense reward underscores the concept of 'Ziyarah' not merely as a physical act but as a profound spiritual connection to the Ahl al-Bayt, serving as a means of expiation and closeness to God. The number eighty likely signifies completeness or a high degree of merit, reflecting the centrality of the Imam's sacrifice in Shia theology.
